scope: Personal design-stage reinspection of the selected primary edition. These observations supplement the source and grammar auditors; they do not replace the later independent review of all displayed cells.

checks.source: Cook First Book, selected 1895 second edition
observations: The interrogative table distinguishes the common-person and neuter columns; its instrumental is separate from the assigned NGDA scope.

The ordinary ān/sum, ǣnig, nān/nǣnig, each/either/neither/other/such families are explicitly described as strong-adjective forms. A complete family listing does not itself assign production of every member.

Cook explicitly lists āwiht/ōht anything, nāwiht/nōht nothing and the -hwega compounds as indeclinable. This is Cook’s simplified description, not a claim that all historical wiht-compounds lack oblique inflection. The final grammatical scope assigns nāwiht only as a bounded accusative object, āwiht as a supplied accusative, and the prior exact hwæthwega as supplied support.

checks.source: Cook First Book, selected 1895 second edition
observations: Indefinite hwā and compounds take the interrogative inflection; a new indefinite meaning does not require duplicate ordinary form identities.
The free-relative family is formed with swā … swā. This morphological statement does not make every following verb automatically subjunctive; the unit gives the contingent context explicitly.
Impersonal man is restricted here to nominative singular. Its scope stays separate from the already taught count-noun mann paradigm.

checks.source: Cook First Book, selected 1895 second edition
observations: The negative past be-table supports næs, nǣre and nǣron in their separate indicative positions, with the optative kept in a different column.

The willan table supplies negative present nel(l)e, nelt/nylt and nellað/nyllað, and past nolde/noldon with the ordinary past endings. Selected variants must be declared; identical surfaces can occupy different person or mood positions.
The old supplied subjunctive nolde must retain its identity and scope when the new full negative indicative is taught.
All 50 current English prompts were compared again with the images after the final source corrections.
30.6 reads he shall be called great (micel); 30.12 reads If they can. The initial independent witness remains unchanged, and final targets must use the repaired source.
Superseded observation from the lower-resolution pass: the hint was read as blōstnian. The following600dpi reinspection corrects that audit reading; the initial independent witness is preserved.
The higher-resolution source clearly prints blōstmian with m. The earlier n was a transcription mistake in the audit, not a Cook error or alternate printed lemma.
The final exact prompt, both selected model tokens, and the plain/inflected infinitive identities use blōstmian/blōstmianne. The independent initial witness remains unchanged.

prior_teaching_boundary: The paths of reused primary images are storage locations only. No archived or earlier analytical claim is inherited as teaching. Actual active contracts and registers determine every prerequisite.
